kh-ext-sen-monorom-market-food-stalls.basis: the market alleyway: a few stalls do rice with pork, chicken or egg for US$1 to 1.5

la-ext-blue-lagoon-1.basis: Wikipedia: Tham Phu Kham, a cave north-west of Vang Vieng whose name means Blue Lagoon, with a reclining bronze Buddha in the main cave. Wikivoyage: Tham Poukham (Blue Lagoon), a spring-fed lagoon 7 km west of town, 08:00 to 18:00

add.org: Wikipedia — Bokeo Nature Reserve (Nam Kan National Protected Area)

la-ext-bokeo-gibbon.basis: the operator's Classic tour page: three days and two nights in treehouses inside Nam Kan National Park, with trekking and ziplining and the best chance of hearing gibbons. Wikipedia: the reserve that holds the project

add.org: Tourism Laos — Caves (Tham Pa Fa, Khammouane)

la-ext-buddha-cave-thakhek.basis: Tourism Laos: Tham Pa Fa near Na Khang Xang village, Thakhek District, where a villager found 229 Buddha statues in April 2004; a small entrance fee. Wikivoyage: Tham Nong Pafa, often called the Buddha Cave, reached by an elevated walkway and concrete steps

la-ext-coffee-bolaven-tad-champee.basis: Tad Champee, 38 km from Pakse, with a bridge downstream and signs for safe swimming (the page gives a 30,000 kip entry; the card says 10,000 to 20,000)

la-ext-don-khong-island.basis: the island's own article: Khong Island (Don Khong), the largest island and the administrative seat of the Si Phan Don archipelago, 18 km long

la-ext-dondet-bungalows.basis: dozens of Don Det guesthouses from 50,000 kip with basic bungalows, a porch and a hammock; the sunset side suits the party crowd and the south the quieter stays

https://discoverlaos.today.org: Discover Laos Today — Tad Katamtok Waterfall

la-ext-katamtok.basis: one of the most spectacular and least-visited falls on the Bolaven loop, plunging into a deep jungle valley and largely undeveloped. The page puts it in Sekong Province, about 47 km east of Paksong (the card says Paksong)

la-ext-luangprabang-hostels.basis: Budget list: dorm beds, family-run guesthouses and a backpackers guesthouse ten minutes from the night market

la-ext-luangprabang-resort.basis: Splurge list: Amantaka in the former French hospital, the Apsara in a restored colonial building over the Khan River, and Lotus Villa, a Lao-colonial villa in the UNESCO precinct

la-ext-mekong-slowboat.basis: the two-day slow boat to Luang Prabang stops at Pak Beng for the night, one departure a day around 09:00 to 10:00 (the page gives 200,000 kip to Pak Beng and 400,000 to Luang Prabang, Dec 2024)

https://www.tourismlaos.org.org: Tourism Laos — Luang Prabang Province (Phousi Mountain)

la-ext-mount-phousi.basis: Tourism Laos: 328 zigzag steps up Luang Prabang's holy mountain to the 20 m Wat Chomsi stupa and a 360 degree view. Wikipedia: the hill's own article, 100 m high, between the Mekong and the Nam Khan

https://www.tourismlaos.org.org: Tourism Laos — Luang Namtha Province (Nam Ha National Protected Area)

add.org: Wikipedia — Nam Ha National Protected Area

la-ext-namha-trek.basis: Tourism Laos: day and overnight treks and kayaking in Nam Ha NPA, with stays in jungle camps, an eco-lodge or village homestays, booked in Luang Namtha town; the Nalan trail to a Khmu village. Wikipedia: the protected area, an ecotourism destination

la-ext-nongkhiaw-homestay.basis: tour offices and guesthouses in Nong Khiaw offer one to three day treks and homestays; the page does not name a village host

la-ext-pakse-bolaven-coffee-tour.basis: Champasak Province: Pakse is an hour from Lao coffee country, with coffee tours and cafes, and a plantation visit ends in tastings (Tad Fane entry)

la-ext-pakse-daoheuang-food.basis: Dao Heuang Market, Road 38, with many food stalls; Talat Dao Heuang (the New Market) is listed about 2 km south-east of town

la-ext-pakse-town-guesthouses.basis: Pakse's Sleep section lists the town's hotels and guesthouses, among them the Arawan Riverside Hotel on the Mekong

la-ext-paksong-market-food.basis: Paksong's market has noodle and barbecue eateries, sandwiches, blended fruit drinks and baguettes; its Coffee note adds that good coffee is sold at the market

https://www.tourismlaos.org.org: Tourism Laos — Vientiane Capital (Patuxay, Victory Monument)

la-ext-patuxai.basis: Tourism Laos: the Patuxay memorial monument on Lanexang Avenue, built in 1957 (Wikipedia gives 1957 to 1968), with a climb to a panoramic view. Wikipedia: the monument's own article

add.org: Tourism Laos — Xieng Khouang Province (Jar Site 2)

la-ext-plain-of-jars-2.basis: Tourism Laos: Jar Site 2, or Ban Na Kho, in Phaxay district with 93 jars on two hills (the page gives 20 km and, elsewhere, 25 km from Phonsavan). Wikipedia: sites 1, 2 and 3 are open to visitors. Wikivoyage: Site 2 entry 30,000 kip

la-ext-rental-vang-vieng.basis: bicycles for 60,000 kip a day, electric scooters and motorbikes for 170,000 to 200,000 kip a day, and a warning to check the bike and the contract; the page does not name buggies

https://www.tourismlaos.org.org: Tourism Laos — Luang Prabang Province (Royal Palace Museum)

add.org: Wikipedia — Royal Palace, Luang Prabang (Haw Kham)

la-ext-royal-palace-museum-lpb.basis: Tourism Laos: the Royal Palace Museum, first built in 1904 in the French colonial era, with the Prabang Buddha image. Wikipedia: the palace (Haw Kham), built in 1904 and converted to the national museum

add.org: Wikipedia (Lao) — ຫໍພິພິດທະພັນໄດໂນເສົາ

la-ext-savannakhet-dinosaur-museum.basis: Lao article: the dinosaur museum about 500 m from Wat Xaisomboun (no English article exists); it gives hours of 8:00-12:00 and 13:00-14:00, where the card says 13:00 to 16:00. Wikivoyage: daily 08:00-11:30 and 13:30-16:30, bones from Xonbouly District

https://discoverlaos.today.org: Discover Laos Today — Tad Yuang Waterfall (Nguang Waterfall)

la-ext-tad-yuang.basis: Discover Laos Today: Tad Yuang, also called Nguang, near Paksong with viewing points and a picnic area. Tourism Laos: twin torrents falling about 40 m into jungle, swimming at the bottom allowed

https://www.taeclaos.org.org: Traditional Arts and Ethnology Centre — Visitor information

la-ext-taec-lpb.basis: the museum's own visitor page: a small museum of Lao ethnic cultures with a fair-trade shop and boutique, about an hour's visit, beside Dara Market. Tourism Laos: open daily except Monday, 09:00 to 18:00

la-ext-talat-sao.basis: Wikipedia: the market's own article, a two-storey morning market at Lan Xang Road, open 07:00 to about 16:00. Tourism Laos: Talat Sao for textiles, silks and decorative pieces

la-ext-thakhek-night-market-food.basis: night food stalls at the far end of the main road sell pancakes and pork buns by lamplight, with baguette stands near the new fountain square; the page names no grills or noodle soups

la-ext-thakhek-square-guesthouses.basis: Thakhek's Sleep list: city-centre hotels and guesthouses near the Mekong, such as the Inthira on Anou Road; the square itself is named in the Eat section

add.org: Tourism Laos — Vientiane Province (Tham Chang Cave)

la-ext-tham-chang-cave.basis: Wikipedia: Tham Jang, south-west of Vang Vieng, reached by a bridge over the Nam Song and a long flight of steps, with a spring about 50 m inside. Tourism Laos: Tham Chang (or Jung), Vang Vieng's most important cave

https://www.tourismlaos.org.org: Tourism Laos — Vientiane Capital (That Dam, Black Stupa)

la-ext-that-dam-vientiane.basis: Tourism Laos: the Black Stupa in a roundabout near Talat Sao, about 500 years old, once gilded, with the gold stripped by Siamese invaders. Wikipedia: the stupa between Chantha Khoumane and Bartholoni roads, said to hold a seven-headed naga

add.org: Wikipedia (Lao) — ພຣະທາດ ອິງຮັງ

la-ext-that-ing-hang.basis: Lao article: a sacred stupa about 12 km from town, built in the 16th century (no English article exists). Wikivoyage: 13 km north-east of Savannakhet, 16th century, with the Boun Pha festival each December

la-ext-vangvieng-outdoors.basis: Tourism Laos: Vang Vieng's limestone caves and watersports such as kayaking and tubing. Wikipedia: adventure sports and karst scenery, inner tubing and kayaking on the Nam Song. Wikivoyage: kayaking, tubing and cave visits (the intro adds ziplines and hot-air balloons)

la-ext-vangvieng-riverside-guesthouses.basis: Vang Vieng's Sleep list includes river-view bungalows (Champa Lao Bungalow on the island) and the Elephant Crossing Hotel, whose rooms face the river

la-ext-vientiane-ban-anou-night-market.basis: Ban Anou Night Market: some of the best cheap meals in the city although only about a block long, setting up at sundown with street snacks

la-ext-vientiane-longstay.basis: Mid-range list names Somerset Vientiane, 116 studio, one and two bedroom apartments; the page names no condo market

https://www.tourismlaos.org.org: Tourism Laos — Vientiane Capital (Settha Palace Hotel)

la-ext-vientiane-settha-palace.basis: the hotel's own page: built circa 1932 and restored. Wikipedia: a renovated French colonial building from 1932, reopened in 1999. Tourism Laos: a boutique hotel since 1932

la-ext-wat-phou-champasak-town.basis: the town's own article: a small town on the west bank of the Mekong about 40 km south of Pakse (its coordinates, 14.84 N 105.75 E, are about 14 km from the card's)

la-ext-wat-sisaket.basis: Tourism Laos: built in 1818 by King Anouvong in the centre of the old city, the only ancient temple left intact after 1828. Wikipedia: the temple on Lan Xang Road, with a cloister wall of more than 2,000 Buddha images and a museum

https://whc.unesco.org.org: UNESCO World Heritage — Town of Luang Prabang

la-ext-wat-xieng-thong.basis: UNESCO: Wat Xieng Thong, from the 16th century, the most complex ensemble of the town pagodas. Tourism Laos: built 1559 to 1560 by King Say Setthathirath, open daily 08:00 to 17:00. Wikipedia: the temple on the northern tip of the peninsula

open.th-ext-nan-walking-street: No checkable page (2026-10-18): TAT's only page for Kad Khuang Muang Nan is a 2023 one-off food fair at another site, and blogs disagree on the days (Saturday only vs Friday to Sunday).
open.vi-ext-cannon-fort-cat-ba: No checkable page (2026-10-18): no Wikipedia article; Wikivoyage Cat Ba and the 303 vietnam.travel pages read for D5 do not name the fort.
open.vi-ext-con-dao-con-son-market-evening-st: No checkable page (2026-10-18): Wikivoyage Con Dao names only the early-morning fruit and vegetable market in Con Son town, and vietnam.travel names no evening stalls.
open.vi-ext-dalat-nightmarket-banhtrangnuong: No checkable page (2026-10-18): vietnam.travel's Da Lat pages and Wikivoyage Da Lat do not name the night market; English Wikipedia's banh trang nuong article says only that the dish is popular in Da Lat.
open.vi-ext-hue-herbal-sauna: No checkable page (2026-10-18): vietnam.travel's herbal-bath pages are about the Red Dao baths in Sa Pa and Hoang Su Phi; nothing names a Hue royal herbal bath.
open.vi-ext-ninhbinh-cho-rong: No checkable page (2026-10-18): Wikivoyage Ninh Binh mentions "the main market across the bridge" without naming it; vietnam.travel does not name it.
open.vi-ext-tavan-cau-may: No checkable page (2026-10-18): Vietnamese Wikipedia has only a red link for Cầu Mây (Sa Pa); Sapa O'Chau's treks mention a hanging bridge but not this one by name.
open.vi-ext-tavan-giang-ta-chai-waterfall: No checkable page (2026-10-18): Sapa O'Chau's treks name the walk from Ta Van through bamboo to Giang Ta Chai but not the waterfall; no Wikipedia or Wikivoyage entry.
open.kh-ext-koh-trong: No checkable page (2026-10-19): no Wikipedia article; Wikivoyage Kratie does not name the island; Tourism Cambodia names Koh Trong Island only as the address of one hotel (Rajabori Villas) in its Kratie stay list.
open.kh-ext-koh-trong-homestays: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Tourism Cambodia's Kratie stay list names Koh Trong Island only as a hotel address and its homestay page names no Kratie homestays; Wikivoyage Kratie does not name the island.
open.kh-ext-koh-rong-long-set-beach: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Koh Rong has a Long Set Beach section, but it is the 7 km west-coast strand ending at Sok San (the other Koh Rong beach card) and puts the beach on the sunset side where this card says east; no page names 4K Beach. The two cards may be one beach.
open.kh-ext-siem-reap-road60-night-market: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Siem Reap and Tourism Cambodia's Siem Reap pages do not name a Road 60 night market (Road 60 appears only in a hotel address).
open.kh-ext-battambang-riverside-stalls: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Battambang and Tourism Cambodia's Battambang eat page name no riverside evening stalls (Wikivoyage warns that streets go dark after 19:00).
open.la-ext-nongkhiaw-bridge-food: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Nong Khiaw (Eat) lists restaurants beside the bridge but no evening food-stall strip, and its Muang Ngoi Neua page adds none; the stalls have no article of their own.
open.la-ext-pakse-ban-tong-night-market: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Pakse names no riverside night market (its Eat section lists restaurants and Dao Heuang Market), and the Tourism Laos Champasak Province page names none.
open.la-ext-paksong-plateau-lodges: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Paksong (Sleep) lists three guesthouses and a hotel in town, and Wikivoyage Bolaven Plateau lists no lodge or homestay, so no page names farm homestays among the coffee plots.
open.la-ext-phosy-market: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Luang Prabang describes a Morning Market on the inner road by the National Museum and a Night Market, and does not name Phosy Market; there is no article of its own.
open.la-ext-si-phan-don-don-det-sunset-strip-: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Don Det (Eat) names individual restaurants, but no sunset-side Lao kitchens on stilts; there is no article of its own.
open.la-ext-vangvieng-riverside-food: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Vang Vieng (Eat) mentions pancake and sandwich stalls and a food court, not a riverside charcoal-grill night market; there is no article of its own.
open.la-ext-vientiane-herbal-sauna: No checkable page (2026-10-19): Wikivoyage Vientiane names no herbal sauna (its one Sok Paluang Road line is about a swimming pool), the Tourism Laos Vientiane Capital page has none, and the pages that describe it are commercial travel sites.
open.la-ext-vientiane-khao-piak-sen-shops: No checkable page (2026-10-19): English Wikipedia's Khao piak sen article describes the dish and names no Vientiane shop, and Wikivoyage Vientiane lists noodle shops 'all over town' without naming khao piak sen.
